mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes autosomes from sex chromosomes in humans?

options.A: Autosomes determine gender, while sex chromosomes are identical in both sexes
options.B: Autosomes are the same in both males and females, whereas sex chromosomes differ (XX in females, XY in males)
options.C: Autosomes are only found in females, sex chromosomes only in males
options.D: Autosomes are larger than sex chromosomes in all cases

mcqs.answer: Autosomes are the same in both males and females, whereas sex chromosomes differ (XX in females, XY in males)
mcqs.explanation: Autosomes are the 22 pairs of non‑sex chromosomes and are identical in composition in males and females. Sex chromosomes are the X and Y chromosomes; females have two X chromosomes (XX) and males have one X and one Y (XY). Options A, C and D contain incorrect statements about the role and distribution of these chromosomes.

mcqs.question: A male (XY) fertilizes an egg that contains only an X chromosome. What are the possible chromosomal make‑ups of the offspring and their corresponding sexes?
mcqs.explanation: The egg always contributes an X chromosome. The sperm can contribute either an X or a Y. X (egg) + X (sperm) gives XX, which develops as a female; X (egg) + Y (sperm) gives XY, which develops as a male. Options B, C, and D describe impossible or non‑viable combinations for human sex determination.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares the chromosomal contribution of the egg and the sperm in human sex determination?

options.A: Both sperm and egg always contribute an X chromosome, so sex is determined by environmental factors
options.B: The egg always contributes an X chromosome, while the sperm can contribute either an X or a Y chromosome, determining the sex of the zygote
options.C: The sperm always contributes an X chromosome, while the egg can contribute either X or Y, determining sex
options.D: Both sperm and egg can contribute either X or Y chromosomes, making sex determination a 50% chance for each gender

mcqs.answer: The egg always contributes an X chromosome, while the sperm can contribute either an X or a Y chromosome, determining the sex of the zygote
mcqs.explanation: In humans, the oocyte (egg) carries only an X chromosome. The sperm carries either an X or a Y chromosome. The combination X (egg) + X (sperm) yields a female (XX); X (egg) + Y (sperm) yields a male (XY). Options A, C, and D misstate the gametic contributions.

mcqs.question: A normal male (XY) is crossed with a female having Turner syndrome (XO). Which of the following best describes the expected genotypic and phenotypic distribution among viable offspring?

options.A: 1/4 XX normal females, 1/4 XY normal males, 1/4 XO Turner females, 1/4 OY non‑viable
options.B: 1/2 XX normal females and 1/2 XY normal males (no Turner offspring)
options.C: 1/2 XY males and 1/2 XO Turner females (no normal females)
options.D: All offspring are non‑viable because of chromosomal imbalance

mcqs.answer: 1/4 XX normal females, 1/4 XY normal males, 1/4 XO Turner females, 1/4 OY non‑viable
mcqs.explanation: The XO female can contribute either an X chromosome or no sex chromosome (O). The XY male can contribute X or Y. Viable combinations are: X (female) + X (male) = XX (normal female); X + Y = XY (normal male); O + X = XO (Turner female). The O + Y = OY combination is non‑viable. Hence among all conceptions the ratio is 1 : 1 : 1 : 1, with the OY embryos not surviving. Options B, C, and D ignore the XO possibility or incorrectly state viability.
